text: “You want money?” “No, indeed, I have plenty in hand.” “There never was such a Dame Durden,” said my guardian, “for making money last.” He had laid down his pen and leaned back in his chair looking at me. I have often spoken of his bright face, but I thought I had never seen it look so bright and good. There was a high happiness upon it which made me think, “He has been doing some great kindness this morning.” “There never was,” said my guardian, musing as he smiled upon me, “such a Dame Durden for making money last.” He had never yet altered his old manner. I loved it and him so much that when I now went up to him and took my usual chair, which was always put at his side—for sometimes I read to him, and sometimes I talked to him, and sometimes I silently worked by him—I hardly liked to disturb it by laying my hand on his breast. But I found I did not disturb it at all.
